content: Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of amitriptyline by inhibiting the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. It is recommended to use caution and monitor the patient closely. Antidepressants should be carefully titrated to achieve the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible initial or maintenance dose, and monitoring for antidepressant response during coadministration with cobicistat. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of amlodipine by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of amoxapine by inhibiting the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Antidepressants should be carefully titrated to achieve the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose, and monitoring for response during coadministration with cobicistat. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of apalutamide by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. While initial dosage modification is not required when coadministering apalutamide with strong CYP3A4 or CYP2C8 inhibitors, dose reduction may be necessary based on tolerability. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of apixaban by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of aripiprazole by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. The aripiprazole dose should be reduced by 25%, and by approximately 50% if coadministered with both a CYP3A4 inhibitor and a CYP2D6 inhibitor. Cobicistat can decrease the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Monitor for potential decreases in antimalarial efficacy or QT prolongation. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of atogepant by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. The recommended atogepant dosage is 10 mg orally once daily when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of atorvastatin by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors that are not contraindicated with cobicistat, the dose should not exceed 20 mg/day. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of avatrombopag by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. When treating immune thrombocytopenia (ITP), coadministration with moderate or strong dual CYP2C9/3A4 inhibitors requires a decreased avatrombopag starting dose. Refer to the drug monograph for specific recommendations. Belzutifan can decrease the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. If coadministration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates cannot be avoided, consider increasing the dose of the sensitive CYP3A4 substrate in accordance with its prescribing information. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of benzhydrocodone/acetaminophen by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Cobicistat can increase the levels of berotralstat, a BCRP substrate, by other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects when coadministered with a BCRP inhibitor. Cobicistat can increase the levels of betrixaban by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Decrease the betrixaban dose to 80 mg orally once, followed by 40 mg orally daily if coadministered with a P-gp inhibitor. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of bortezomib by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Bosentan can decrease the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Dose reduction of bosentan is required. Refer to the prescribing information for recommended dosage adjustments. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of brentuximab vedotin by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of brexpiprazole by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Administer half the usual brexpiprazole dose when coadministered with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. If coadministered with a moderate CYP2D6 inhibitor plus a strong/moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor, administer a quarter of the brexpiprazole dose. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of bromocriptine by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of budesonide by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of buprenorphine by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. For patients on buprenorphine subdermal implants, monitor for signs of overmedication if CYP3A4 inhibitors are newly initiated. Implant removal may be necessary if dose adjustments are not feasible. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of buspirone by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. A decreased dose of buspirone may be required. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of calcifediol by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. CYP450 inhibitors may alter vitamin D metabolism, potentially affecting serum calcifediol levels and its conversion to calcitriol. Dose adjustment of calcifediol may be required, and serum 25-hydroxyvitamin D, intact PTH, and calcium concentrations should be closely monitored. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of cannabidiol by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Consider reducing the cannabidiol dose when coadministered with a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of capmatinib by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of carbamazepine by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of cariprazine by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Coadministration with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors requires cariprazine dose reduction. Refer to the drug monograph for dosage modification instructions. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of carvedilol by inhibiting the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Cenobamate can decrease the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Increase the dose of CYP3A4 substrates as needed when coadministered with cenobamate. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of chlordiazepoxide by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of ciclesonide inhaled by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of cilostazol by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Reduce the cilostazol dose to 50 mg twice daily when coadministered and monitor for cilostazol-related adverse effects. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of citalopram by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of clomipramine by inhibiting the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Antidepressants should be carefully titrated to achieve the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose, and monitoring for response during coadministration with cobicistat. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of clonazepam by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Clinical monitoring is recommended when coadministered with anticonvulsants. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of clorazepate by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Adjust the dose of clorazepate if necessary. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of colchicine by other mechanisms. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Coadministration with colchicine is contraindicated in patients with renal and/or hepatic impairment due to the potential for serious or life-threatening reactions. Dosage adjustment of colchicine may be necessary upon coadministration with cobicistat. Refer to colchicine prescribing information for dosing instructions. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of cyclosporine by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of dabigatran by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. For atrial fibrillation, avoid coadministration of dabigatran with P-gp inhibitors if CrCl <30 mL/min. For DVT/PE treatment, avoid coadministration if CrCl <50 mL/min. Danazol can increase the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of dapsone by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of darifenacin by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Administer 5 mg orally when coadministered. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of darolutamide by other mechanisms. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Darolutamide is a P-gp and CYP3A4 substrate. Monitor closely for increased adverse reactions and modify the dose of darolutamide as needed when coadministered with drugs that are both P-gp and strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of dasatinib by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Dosage adjustment of dasatinib may be necessary upon coadministration with cobicistat coadministered with atazanavir or darunavir. Refer to dasatinib prescribing information for dosing instructions. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of deflazacort by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Decrease the deflazacort dose to one-third of the recommended dose if coadministered with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of desipramine by inhibiting the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Antidepressants should be carefully titrated to achieve the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose, and monitoring for response during coadministration with cobicistat. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of diazepam by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. A decreased dose of diazepam may be required. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of digoxin by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Titrate the digoxin dose by approximately 30-50% or modify the dosing frequency and continue monitoring. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of diltiazem by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of disopyramide by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Clinical monitoring is recommended when coadministered with antiarrhythmics. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of docetaxel by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Consider reducing docetaxel dosing by 50% if concomitant administration cannot be avoided. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of doravirine by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Coadministration of doravirine and CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations and toxicities of doravirine. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of doxepin by inhibiting the hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Antidepressants should be carefully titrated to achieve the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose, and monitoring for response during coadministration with cobicistat. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of dronabinol by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Dronabinol is a CYP3A4 substrate. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of efavirenz by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of elagolix by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Coadministration of elagolix 200 mg BID with strong CYP3A inhibitors for more than one month is not recommended. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of encorafenib by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Encorafenib both inhibits and induces CYP3A4 at clinically relevant plasma concentrations. Coadministration with sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may result in increased toxicity or decreased efficacy of these agents. Cobicistat can increase the toxicity of enfortumab vedotin by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Enfortumab vedotin is an antibody-drug conjugate that releases monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE) via proteolytic cleavage. MMAE is primarily metabolized by CYP3A4 in vitro. Monitor closely for signs of toxicities. Enzalutamide can decrease the levels or effects of cobicistat by inducing the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of erlotinib by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. If coadministration cannot be avoided, reduce the erlotinib dose by 50 mg decrements and monitor for adverse effects. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of escitalopram by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of esomeprazole by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of estradiol vaginal by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase plasma concentrations of estrogens and toxicities. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of ethosuximide by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Fedratinib can increase the levels or effects of cobicistat by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Adjust the dose of drugs that are CYP3A4 substrates as necessary. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of felodipine by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of fentanyl by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. If coadministration of CYP3A4 inhibitors with fentanyl is necessary, monitor for respiratory depression and sedation at frequent intervals and consider fentanyl dose adjustments until stable drug effects are achieved. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of flecainide by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Clinical monitoring is recommended when coadministered with antiarrhythmics. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of fluoxetine by other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Antidepressants should be carefully titrated to achieve the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose, and monitoring for response during coadministration with SSRIs and cobicistat. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of flurazepam by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Cobicistat can increase the levels of fluticasone furoate by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Cobicistat can increase the levels of fluticasone inhaled by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of fluvastatin by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. For HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors that are not contraindicated with cobicistat, start with the lowest recommended dose and titrate while monitoring for safety. Fluvoxamine can increase the levels or effects of cobicistat by other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Carefully titrate the dose of antidepressants to the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose, and monitor for response during coadministration with SSRIs and cobicistat. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of fostamatinib by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Monitor for toxicities that may require fostamatinib dose reduction. Cobicistat increases levels of gefitinib by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Coadministration of strong CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase the risk of gefitinib adverse effects. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of glecaprevir/pibrentasvir by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of haloperidol by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of hydrocodone by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Coadministration with CYP3A4 inhibitors may increase hydrocodone plasma concentrations, potentially leading to fatal respiratory depression. Cobicistat can decrease the levels or effects of ifosfamide by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. Coadministration of CYP3A4 inhibitors may decrease the metabolism of ifosfamide to its active alkylating metabolites, reducing its efficacy. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of imatinib by inhibiting the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Cobicistat can increase the levels or effects of imipramine by other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor the patient closely. Antidepressants should be carefully titrated to achieve the desired effect, starting with the lowest feasible dose, and monitoring for response during coadministration with cobicistat.
